text:
liam: FYI ran into a parity bug in the python SDK while onboarding a customer. list_endpoints auto-pager stops after a couple pages and we get a 401 from the API.

erin: Can you share the SDK snippet + equivalent curl?

liam: repro:
```py
# sampleapp/collector.py
routes = client.routes.list(limit=100)
for r in routes.auto_paginate():
    process(r)
```

curl works:
`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/routes?limit=100&cursor=page_2"`
returns 200 + header `x-next-cursor: page_3` in REST. SDK expects `next_cursor` in JSON body.

pat: Wait, REST exposes cursor in header now? I thought we moved to `meta.next_cursor` in body last year.

liam: That's the thing  we have two different pagination signals depending on deployment: hosted uses response header `x-next-cursor`, private deployments use `meta.next_cursor`. SDK only handles `body.next_cursor` and `body.meta.next_cursor` but not header. So when hosted returns header-only, SDK treats response as last page and stops, then caller re-requests and eventually token hits a guard and we see 401.

erin: Oof. Another layer: our auth middleware looks for `x-auth-refresh=true` header from the server to rotate ephemeral creds. Hosted currently uses `x-rotate-ephemeral` instead (internal rollout). SDK only honors `x-auth-refresh`.

aj: So two separate incompatibilities: pagination location (header vs body) and auth-refresh header name. Both cause the client to either stop early or never refresh credentials.

liam: I added logs: we see "no next_cursor found, ending pagination" followed by later "401: token invalid" when next request is attempted.

pat: Proposed fix: SDK pager should check (in order) `resp.meta?.next_cursor`, `resp.next_cursor`, then `resp.headers['x-next-cursor']` and normalize into a single cursor. For auth, accept both `x-auth-refresh` and `x-rotate-ephemeral` header names and treat any truthy value as trigger.

liam: Agreed. Also add defensive behavior: don't call next page if cursor is falsy, and surface a debug metric when pagination stops because of unknown shape.

erin: Can we add a tiny compatibility test matrix in CI? Matrix entries: hosted (header cursor + rotate header), private (body meta cursor + auth-refresh header), and legacy (top-level next_cursor). Mock responses in unit tests.

aj: I'll file an SDK board ticket and mark it P1 for the onboarding flow. Add changelog note about header compatibility.

liam: Pushed a WIP: branch `fix/python-sdk-pager-compat` with two failing tests. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk-python/pull/998

devex-bot: CI for sdk-python/pull/998 failed: test_pagination_header_compat raises AssertionError - expected next_page called 3 times but called 1.

pat: That suggests the normalization code didn't read headers in the mocked client. In tests we may be using a fake Response that doesn't populate `.headers` the same way. Add adapter to test harness to set headers and body consistently.

erin: Also audit other list_* endpoints (models, keys, routes) for same drift. Likely the change was rolled piecemeal.

liam: Will run grep for `meta.next_cursor` vs `x-next-cursor` across API docs and samples and produce a one-pager for DX.

aj: After the fix, let's update quickstart sample to show how to handle both pagination styles when people implement custom pagers.

liam: Thanks team. I'll iterate on the PR with the test adjustments. Will post here when green. :rocket:
